quote: So to be honest, Tracy, I do think that you don't have enough sun for solely for solar to work
stewart_read: The rep disqualifies the property off a satellite image alone, before any verify items were captured. There is no shade/tree-coverage criterion defined in dq_rules today — this is a schema gap Ion needs to formalize (what counts as disqualifying shade, and what evidence standard is required before telling a customer their home won't work).
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: the rep may be following an unstated but real Ion policy that satellite-visible heavy tree coverage is an immediate DQ, making this efficient rather than premature. This is not fully supported — the rep never asks about sun hours, seasonal variation, or offers a site-visit alternative, which would be expected even under a real DQ policy.
coaching_implication: Confirm with Kenny whether satellite-only shade assessment is an approved DQ method, and if so, whether reps should still ask 1-2 verifying questions (sun hours, time of day) before delivering the verdict.

quote: It's just kinda hard to see because on Google Maps, all the trees are in the way. So
stewart_read: The rep admits the imagery itself is unclear right after using it to justify a DQ conclusion on the main house. This undercuts the confidence of the initial disqualification and should have prompted the rep to ask the customer directly about sun exposure rather than relying on a visual the rep just admitted was obstructed.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to treat unclear satellite imagery as a cue to ask the customer, not a cue to guess and DQ anyway.

quote: Now the wintertime, it would work perfectly because, like, right now, the sun is shining so brightly into this room.
stewart_read: The customer hands the rep a specific, useful data point about seasonal sun exposure that directly counters the shade concern. The rep responds with a flat 'Mhmm. Okay' and then restates the same shade conclusion without engaging the point.
coaching_implication: This was a moment to slow down and ask a follow-up (what time of day, which windows, how many hours) rather than filing it and repeating the DQ. Replay this exact exchange with the rep.

quote: On the side, you have the other option is on the side of the house. There's no trees there.
stewart_read: This is the customer's third independent attempt to find a workable location on her property (main roof, garage, side yard) — a level of persistence and motivation that most leads never show. The rep's response pivots straight to a ground-mount cost explanation without first asking whether a roof-mount was possible on that side of the house.
coaching_implication: Flag this as a highly motivated lead the rep may have let go too easily. The manager should ask the rep why a roof-mount option on the shade-free side of the house wasn't explored before closing out ground-mount as the only alternative.

quote: just because due to trenching and everything involved. They do tend to get super, super expensive.
stewart_read: The rep offers cost-mechanism detail (trenching expense) that is closer-tier financial reasoning, delivered to justify why an option isn't offered rather than redirecting the customer to a specialist who could actually assess the side-yard roof option.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: the rep may simply be repeating a stock line used to quickly close out ground-mount requests, not consciously overstepping scope. Given the immediate move to DQ with no further probing, reactive is the better-supported read here.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to redirect technical/cost justifications to 'that's something the specialist can walk through on site' rather than delivering the reasoning themselves, especially when it forecloses an option (roof-mount on the shaded-free side) that was never actually evaluated.

quote: We just like to be quick. So Yeah. I like that. I like that.
stewart_read: The rep never states their name after this point clearly, never names the company beyond implicit context, and never explains why they're calling (form-fill, referral, etc.) before moving straight into the address verification. Legitimacy is assumed rather than established.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: since the customer self-identified as having just filled out a form and called Ion herself, minimal intro may be reasonable because legitimacy is already established by her own action. This has some support given her opening line, but the rep still never introduces themself by name or states the company name aloud on this transcript.
coaching_implication: Even on inbound-motivated leads, state name and company explicitly for the record and for rapport — takes 5 seconds and costs nothing.
